$schema_note: Single source of truth for every material tag string this project's Python side (src/procedural/mesh_factory.py, src/procedural/building_placement.py) can emit as a Mesh.material value. tests/unit/test_material_tags_coverage.py asserts every emittable tag has an entry here. The C++ side (unreal_plugin/.../ProceduralMesh/MaterialResolver.cpp) is hand-authored against this same file rather than parsing it at runtime -- see KNOWN_GAPS_AND_ISSUES.md for why (no cross-language codegen for this scope). Asset paths are real City Sample content, verified present and dependency-traced in CitySample before being chosen -- not guessed -- but still require the same one-time manual Migrate step already documented for Vehicle/Traffic content (see KNOWN_GAPS_AND_ISSUES.md).

stucco.used_by: building_placement.py BUILDING_MATERIALS_BY_TYPE[RESIDENTIAL] -- no dedicated stucco asset exists in City Sample's kit; a painted-smooth-stone finish is the closest real visual match

concrete.used_by: building_placement.py BUILDING_MATERIALS_BY_TYPE[MIXED_USE, COMMERCIAL]; also mesh_factory.py's Building.material default

vehicle_paint.used_by: mesh_factory.py MeshFactory.build_vehicle_mesh -- dead in the real generation pipeline since City Sample Phase 1 (vehicles now spawn as real assets via the "assets" JSON array, not procedural boxes via "meshes"), kept resolvable for the validator tests that still exercise it directly. A generic painted-metal instance is a reasonable proxy for flat car paint; not worth a dedicated car-paint asset for dead code.

pedestrian.used_by: mesh_factory.py MeshFactory.build_pedestrian_mesh -- pedestrians are still plain boxes (see KNOWN_GAPS_AND_ISSUES.md's Phase 6 gating), so this is a distinct placeholder color, not a real clothing/skin material
